title: Model provenance, runtime gating, and lightweight compatibility flags for onboarding community weights
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: We onboard an increasing number of community/open models into the catalog. Current intake captures basic metadata but lacks structured provenance (origin, build artifacts), deterministic compatibility signals, and runtime gating to prevent unanticipated runtime failures or quality regressions when a new variant is enabled in hosted or dedicated deployments.

Problem statement: Without provenance and lightweight runtime gating, customers and runtime teams face surprises: model variants that fail at runtime due to kernel incompatibilities, models that later are discovered to be retracted upstream, or variants that degrade quality for high-SLO customers. We need a concise PRD that defines: (1) required provenance fields and artifact checks during intake, (2) a small set of compatibility flags that the runtime can use to decide safe fallbacks, and (3) an automated gating flow for enabling new open model variants in production with rollback thresholds.

Goals:
- Define a minimal provenance schema for community/open model intake that is enforceable at admission time and recorded in the model catalog.
- Define a small, operational set of compatibility flags (semantic, runtime, quantization-sanity) that map to runtime gating policies.
- Define an onboarding gating flow with automated tests, canary windows, and rollback rules that the Console and Dedicated control planes can automate.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement full binary-level attestation or cryptographic signing of artifacts (we will propose that as a follow-up).
- We are not defining a new heavy formal compatibility matrix; instead we want a compact set of flags and numeric thresholds that guide automation and operator triage.
requirements:
1) Provenance: intake must capture: source_url (string), upstream_tag_or_release (string), model_checksum (sha256 string), build_recipe_link (optional), declared_license (string), declared_owner_contact (email), and provenance_notes (string). Intake should reject entries missing source_url or model_checksum.

2) Artifact validation: on intake, compute sha256 of the stored artifact, verify it matches model_checksum; store mismatch as 'artifact_integrity: failed' and mark intake 'blocked' until resolved.

3) Compatibility flags (minimal set):
- runtime_compat: values ["native", "quantized_compatible", "partial"] with short meaning: native=expected to run on common kernels; quantized_compatible=expected to work when quantized (8bit/4bit); partial=needs special path.
- semantic_stability: values ["stable", "experimental", "untested"]; drives rollout aggressiveness.
- kernel_requirements: list-of-strings (e.g., "flash_attention_v2", "fused_gelu") - runtime will check kernel availability.
- max_seq_tested: integer (declares longest validated sequence length).

4) Runtime gating policy: mapping from flags to runtime behavior, configurable per-customer tier:
- If runtime_compat=="native" AND semantic_stability in ["stable","experimental"] => allow soft-canary (1% traffic) then scale to target.
- If runtime_compat=="quantized_compatible" AND customer_prefers_quantized==true => run canary on quantized path only.
- If kernel_requirements contains items not available in region/hardware => mark as 'requires_compat_fallback' and set default routing to fallback_model_id until explicitly enabled.

5) Automated test suite for intake: must include model load check within the same runtime used in production, sample-generation smoke test (<= 512 tokens), and a small set of prompts (provided by catalog intake) to measure logits stability and tokenization sanity. Pass thresholds to define semantic_stability assignment.

6) Acceptance metadata: each catalog entry must include a recommended pinning policy string (options: always_pin, soft_pin_with_fallback, unpinned) and a human-readable remediation note when intake flags issues.

7) Console integration: intake UI must surface provenance fields, computed artifact_integrity result, compatibility flags, and provide one-click 'enable canary' with suggested canary parameters.

8) Audit trail: every gating decision, manual override, or artifact re-ingestion must be logged and queryable (who, when, reason, commit/PR link).
acceptance_criteria: Provenance schema documented in Confluence and added as required fields in the intake API spec.
Artifact validation implemented on intake (sha256 check) with failure state visible in the catalog entry UI.
Compatibility flags defined and mapped to a runtime policy document (table mapping flag combinations to default gating rules).
Automated intake test suite (load + 3 smoke prompts + seq length check) running in CI for each new community model intake with pass/fail recorded on the catalog entry.
Console shows one-click enable canary flow that pre-populates canary params based on semantic_stability and runtime_compat flags.

Rollback rules defined: if canary error rate > 5% OR quality regression > 6 points on our eval metric during canary window, auto-disable and route to fallback model and create incident ticket template.
Audit logs surface: intake artifact checksum, who enabled canary, canary start/end timestamps, and reason for manual overrides in the entry timeline.
success_metrics: Reduction in runtime ingestion incidents due to missing kernel support by 80% within first quarter after rollout.
Number of catalog entries with complete provenance metadata >= 95% within 6 weeks.
Mean time to detect and roll back a problematic community model during canary <= 15 minutes (automated detection + action).
Decrease in manual triage time per new model intake by 40% (due to clearer flags and automated checks).
proposed_solution:
- Intake API: extend POST /models with the minimal provenance fields and require model_checksum and source_url. The API returns detailed validation results and a 'provisioning_state' (draft, blocked, canary_ready, active, deprecated).

- Compatibility classifier: a lightweight deterministic rule engine run during intake that assigns semantic_stability and runtime_compat based on test suite results plus declared metadata. We will avoid an ML classifier in this phase.

- Runtime mapping: extend model metadata with 'routing_policy' derived from flags and a 'fallback_model_id' default. The serving runtime already supports fallback routing; we add the default selection logic.

- Console and Dedicated control planes: add UI hooks to show flags and to trigger the canary flow. The canary controller will use existing rollout abstractions but add additional health checks tied to artifact_integrity and smoke test results.

- Audit: use existing audit-log pipeline; add a new event type 'model_onboard_gating_action' and ensure it contains the provenance fields and checksum.

Deliverables: intake API changes, small intake-test harness (Python script + job), compatibility mapping doc, Console canary UI change, and audit event addition.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (internal pilot, 2 weeks): enforce provenance fields on internal intake only; run intake validation and attach flags but do not enable canaries automatically.

Phase 2 (closed beta, 4 weeks): enable canary flow for 10 trusted customers and Dedicated hosts in 2 regions. Track metrics and iterate on thresholds.

Phase 3 (general availability): require provenance for all community models; enable default canary policies for hosted catalog entries. Provide migration guide and backfill tooling for existing entries.

Rollback plan: automated disable + route traffic to fallback_model_id on threshold breach; create incident ticket via template and notify catalog team channel. Manual re-enable requires an explicit two-person approval (PM + Eng).
open_questions: What exact eval metric and threshold should be used for 'quality regression' during canary (currently proposing absolute delta of 6 points on the default readability/utility eval).
Should we require signed artifacts for models hosted outside our storage (follow-up work)?
What is the canonical source to prefer when multiple source_url values are provided (GitHub release vs hub release vs direct S3)?
Do we add an automated weekly re-check of provenance URLs to detect upstream retractions or license changes?

implementation_risks: - False positives from the smoke test could block viable models; mitigated by allowing manual override with audit trail.\n- Large artifacts may delay admission due to checksum compute; mitigate by async validation and provisional states.\n- Overly strict gating may slow catalog velocity; we'll monitor and relax thresholds during beta if needed.
